findings.what_happens: crisisDefense reads the defender's statistic through state.killerId or state.victimId. On a player's browser the state is that player's copy of the cast (incident-store.mjs:187-191). The copy of everyone but the killers holds killerId null in a trap, and since 1.2.113 while the killer stands behind a '?'. For the victim's rows defended by the killer (Self-Defense and Role Reversal by Body, Survive by Leg) the browser then answers 0 and shows the base number, with no '+1' line on the tile; the primary GM reads its own cast, finds the killer, and scores the roll against base + 1 when that statistic is 1 or more.
findings.failure_scenario: A trap built by a student with Body 1 springs on Aiko. Her menu and her roll window read Self-Defense 'Beat 18'. She rolls a total of 18. The primary scores 18 against 19 (crisisThreshold at murder-rules.mjs:1773) and the action fails. The stage's promise is one number for the menu, the window and the judge (murder-rules.mjs:232-237). The same gap opens in a direct murder whose opening hid the killer (E69 C8).

Looked for a decision that a trap or a mask drops the defence: none in docs/dev/e64/STATUS.md, the notes or AUDIT 9.2 (docs/dev/e101/REVIEW.md R7 is another point). R3961 hands in a state with both ids, so it stays green. Not run (the audit's rule against running the harness).

findings.title: A GM's room action is closed by the use packet, not by the drawn roll, so a failed roll that is never reported closes nothing
findings.where: scripts/roll-draw.mjs:1174, :1994-2007 (facilityOfDraw asks only whether a use has closed it); scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:136-140 (the row and the public closing are written by facility.use)
findings.what_happens: The rule is that once anyone uses a GM's room action, a failed roll too, it is closed for everyone until the next time of day. The roll is drawn on a payment; the use row and the facilityClosed key are written only when the roller's browser then sends facility.use. An honest browser always sends it. A console that reads a failed drawn roll and sends nothing leaves the action open, for itself and for the table.
findings.failure_scenario: From a player's console: pay one action, throw the Facilities roll of the Dorm's action (drawn on the GM, 9 against 12), send no facility.use; pay again and throw again. Each try costs an action, the action never closes on a failure, and no line of the GMs' record says a roll went unreported. It is the trust model's known shape (a trace an action leaves is placed at the roller's request) and is not in docs/dev/e93/STATUS.md's 'What a console can still do'.

findings.what_happens: A watch has a post only from the Eclipse's start (startWatches) and every watch is dropped at its end (endWatches, on the hook the clock's write fires, 120 to 360 ms after it). A direct murder is declared in an Eclipse and opened only after that Eclipse has ended (eclipse.mjs:520-529: 'LAST, and after the clock has moved'): the opening roll is invited after the GMs' card, the incident's writes and, where no statistic was ruled, a GM's window; and it is drawn on the primary when the killer's player presses Roll, which reads the watch again (roll-draw.mjs:2247).
